choices.explanation: The number of instances alone does not determine processing capacity.

choices.explanation: Check whether shared failure domains are separated.

choices.text: The three-instance option is necessarily more resilient to an AZ failure because it has more instances.
choices.explanation: They share the same AZ failure domain.

choices.text: If instances are in different AZs, there is no need to check the capacity of the one that remains.

choices.text: Costs are the same for every configuration, so there is no need to compare them.

title: Comparing Instance Count and Placement

choices.explanation: Logs provide clues for investigating the cause.

choices.text: Rerun the same check after fixing the issue.
choices.explanation: Confirm the result of the fix.

choices.text: Proceed to deploy even if the check fails.
choices.explanation: A failed check stops subsequent stages.

prompt: When CI fails, select one incorrect response.
title: When CI Fails

prompt: Choose 2 combinations that improve reproducibility when selecting inputs for regression testing tax calculations.

choices.text: Compare the expected result against a fixed clock input, rather than the execution time.
choices.explanation: Fix the execution time as test data so that rerunning the same input lets you confirm that it produces the same result.

choices.text: If the expected result changes each time based on the execution time, also fix the rule for generating it.
choices.explanation: If you retain a time dependency, you must fix both the input time and the rule for generating the expected result.

choices.text: Generate the expected result from the execution result each time.
choices.explanation: If you use the actual result as the expected result, errors cannot be detected.

choices.text: Do not record the input and expected result when a failure occurs.
choices.explanation: Information needed to reproduce the failure is lost.

title: Reproduce results with fixed inputs and expected values

prompt: When setting required conditions for a release gate, choose the two conditions that should stop promotion.

choices.text: A required integration test fails, even if it is only one test.
choices.explanation: A failure in a required check is grounds for preventing progression to the next environment.

choices.text: Type checking fails, and a reproducible log has been saved.
choices.explanation: If type-checking failures are included in the quality criteria, the gate should stop promotion.

choices.text: The wording of an optional description is slightly different.
choices.explanation: Unless it is an explicitly required quality criterion, this may not warrant automatically stopping promotion.

choices.text: All tests passed, so the artifact digest is not checked.
choices.explanation: Passing tests and verifying that the same artifact is being promoted are separate quality criteria.

title: Stop failures at the quality gate

choices.text: Isolate the first mismatch layer by layer, then add a regression test that addresses the cause.
choices.explanation: This identifies the cause and makes recurrence detectable automatically.

choices.text: For IT/E2E, always replace checks of real boundaries with unit mocks alone.
choices.explanation: Integration problems can no longer be detected.

choices.text: Rerun while continuing to share the data from the failed run.
choices.explanation: Data contamination makes the results irreproducible.

choices.text: For IT/E2E, design environment setup, data isolation, and cleanup.
choices.explanation: This verifies real boundaries while keeping the environment reproducible.

choices.text: Record the cause of the failure and any unresolved questions, and use them in the next investigation.
choices.explanation: Recording the results and unresolved questions helps test the next hypothesis and prevent recurrence.

prompt: Choose two incorrect statements about failure investigation and IT/E2E operations.
title: Improving through failures

prompt: The canary error rate exceeds the baseline, and abort criteria were defined in advance. What should you do next?

choices.text: Record that the criteria were exceeded, stop the rollout from expanding, and proceed to investigate or recover.
choices.explanation: Predefined abort criteria are used to control the impact instead of continuing to expand based on intuition.

choices.text: Increase traffic to 100% and dilute the error rate by averaging.
choices.explanation: Expanding while the criteria are exceeded widens the impact.

choices.text: Rewrite the baseline with the new version’s values.
choices.explanation: Changing the baseline to hide an anomaly undermines the basis for observation.

choices.text: Continue based only on the scheduled time without measuring the error rate.
choices.explanation: Staged rollouts are guided by observed values and abort criteria.

title: Observe and apply the abort criteria

prompt: User wait times are increasing, and the queue is growing too. Choose the 2 golden signals to examine together.

choices.text: latency
choices.explanation: Directly captures changes in how long users wait.

choices.text: saturation
choices.explanation: A growing queue may indicate a lack of spare resources or processing capacity.

choices.text: Conclude the cause from traffic alone
choices.explanation: Traffic indicates load, but does not explain both wait times and available capacity.

choices.text: Ignore wait times if error is 0
choices.explanation: Even with no errors, worsening latency affects users.

title: Four ways to look at it: Separate user impact from spare capacity

prompt: When defining an SLO with a target success rate of 99.9%, choose two things that must be explicitly specified.

choices.text: The denominator for the success rate and the observation window
choices.explanation: Without specifying what is counted and over what period it is evaluated, the SLO cannot be reproduced.

choices.text: The alert for exceeding the threshold and how to handle missing data
choices.explanation: Defining the notification conditions and how to handle missing data makes operational decisions consistent.

choices.text: Choose only an SLO name and decide on the denominator later
choices.explanation: Without a defined denominator, the meaning of the success rate changes.

choices.text: Always set alerts for every metric
choices.explanation: Alerts that ignore the purpose and how to handle missing data create noise.

title: SLI, SLO, and alerts: What to notify about, by when, and in what state
